summary.headline: SJS Q1FY27 revenue hit record Rs 2,610 mn (+24.5% YoY) and adjusted PAT Rs 502.5 mn (+45.2%), with EBITDA margin at 30%.
summary.overview: SJS reported its highest-ever quarterly revenue and profitability since listing, with automotive growing 32.4% against 21.7% for the PV plus two-wheeler industry. Reported PAT of Rs 744.2 mn includes a one-time Rs 241.7 mn gain on sale of the old Bangalore facility; adjusted PAT was Rs 502.5 mn (19.3% margin). Management reiterated 1.5x–2x industry outperformance for FY27 and an export target of 14–15% of revenue by FY28. The new SJS Decoplast Pune plant began commercial operations in August 2026, and a wholly-owned cover glass and display subsidiary was approved, with supplies targeted from Q2 FY28.

segments.name: Passenger vehicle
segments.commentary: 44.6% of consolidated revenue; grew 45.4% YoY, but declined QoQ as PV industry fell about 7.5% QoQ on seasonal Q1 softness and Q4 pre-buying.

segments.name: Two-wheeler
segments.commentary: 36.6% of consolidated revenue; grew 19.5% YoY. Hero MotoCorp is a new customer, with cross-selling (e.g., chrome plating) cited as the next growth lever.

segments.name: Consumer appliances and others
segments.commentary: 18.8% of consolidated revenue; management said this segment has lagged and that some low-margin consumer business was traded for higher-margin work at Walter Pack.

segments.name: SJS Decoplast
segments.commentary: Sales have grown about 4x since the Exotech acquisition and EBITDA margin has moved from 12% to 20%. Management targets doubling sales in 3–4 years.

segments.name: Walter Pack India
segments.commentary: Running at about 75% utilisation; export revenue has been flat in a tight range for four quarters while new programmes wait on customer launch decisions.

guidance_outlook: SJS to outperform the underlying automotive industry by 1.5x–2x in FY27.
Export contribution target of 14%–15% of consolidated revenue by FY28; management said advanced discussions should fructify during the year.
FY27 gross margin guidance was 27%–28% EBITDA-level margin range given earlier; management said it is maintaining margins despite about 0.5%–0.6% headwind from input costs this quarter.
Cover glass and display plant supplies to start from Q2 FY28; no firm purchase orders yet, expected after PPAP runs.
Decoplast new capacity to add Rs 200–250 crore revenue over about three years; asset turn 2–2.5x, breakeven at about 1–1.25x asset turn, steady utilisation 85–90% in three years.
Walter Pack non-compete with Walter Pack Spain runs till January 2027.
capex_capacity: SJS Decoplast new Pune facility commenced commercial operations in August 2026; PPAP runs with customers are underway.
Decoplast new capacity adds about Rs 200–250 crore revenue potential, roughly 1.75x existing capacity per analyst; existing capacity is fully utilised.
Cover glass and display plant: equipment on order, to be installed in India, with sales from Q2 FY28; wholly-owned subsidiary approved by board.
Localisation of display content estimated at about 50% (TFT screen imported); TFT investment of USD 4–5 billion not planned.
Capacity expanded at Pune and Bangalore parent plant in the last year; a consolidation phase reviewed capacity and business plans.
demand_pricing: Input cost inflation: management said cost pass-through negotiations with customers are ongoing and some have been agreed; one-quarter to two-quarter lag. Quarterly impact estimated at 0.5%–0.6% of profitability.
Display market in India estimated at Rs 500–1,000 crore, potentially Rs 5,000–7,000 crore by 2030; company aspires to 10% share by 2030.
New order wins cited from Mahindra, Tata Motors, TVS, Autoliv, Royal Enfield, Skoda, John Deere, Hero MotoCorp; SDPL won Tata Motors business and Walter Pack won Mahindra business.
Chrome plating for two-wheelers identified as cross-selling opportunity with existing and new customers.
Pricol is a potential customer for four-wheeler display hardware; SJS has exclusivity for four-wheeler displays with BOE, Pricol's BOE tie-up is for two-wheelers.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin fell about 200 bps QoQ; how long until input cost increases are passed to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins improved; gross margin was 56.7% vs 56.6% in Q4. Raw-material recovery has a one- to two-quarter lag, and the input cost impact was about 0.5%–0.6%.

qa_highlights.question: How much capacity does the new Decoplast plant add, and what asset turn and utilisation to expect?
qa_highlights.answer: Additional revenue potential of Rs 200–250 crore over about three years. Asset turn is expected at 2–2.5x, with 85–90% utilisation in three years. Breakeven at about 1–1.25x asset turn, progressively.

qa_highlights.question: Will SJS get orders for cover glass and display before FY28, and who is the customer interface?
qa_highlights.answer: BOE leads technical development and customer awards; SJS handles local assembly. Formal POs are expected after plant installation and PPAP runs, around FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the PV segment down QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: PV revenue grew 45.3% YoY but declined QoQ as industry PV volumes fell about 7.5% QoQ on soft Q1 seasonality and a Q4 sales push.

qa_highlights.question: Walter Pack and export revenue have been flat for four quarters; when will they ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Export pipeline is in advanced discussions across SJS, Decoplast and Walter Pack, and management expects it to fructify during the year. Walter Pack ramp depends on customer launch decisions.

qa_highlights.question: What is the TAM and margin profile of the cover glass and display business?
qa_highlights.answer: Display TAM in India is Rs 500–1,000 crore now, rising to Rs 5,000–7,000 crore. Margins not yet quantified; management said it would be 10–20% and expects a clearer answer in Q2 FY28.
